rule: Height is one semantic: a step N is the pair --sf-elevation-N--surface and --sf-elevation-N--shadow, and whatever floats above the page takes both. A step's shadow alone leaves a panel flat in the dark theme, where the shadow is black on a near-black page and only the lighter surface shows the height. Components therefore do not use --sf-ui-shadow-N (N 1-5) directly, and a stylesheet that uses a step's shadow also uses that step's surface. The exemptions below are not panels: they keep a colour that carries meaning, which a raised surface would overwrite.
rim: --sf-shadow--rim is the last layer of every step's shadow, off by default (0 0 0 0 transparent). A theme may switch it on to outline raised panels in the dark.
utility: elevation-N sets the pair; shadow-N stays a shadow alone, for an element whose own fill carries meaning.

exemptions.reason: The drag ghost is a copy of the dragged element and keeps that element's own fill; a raised surface would repaint it.
The toggle knob sits on its track and keeps its own colour; it is a control part, not a panel.
The value tooltip is painted by the tooltip role (inverse or surface-1), which a raised surface would overwrite.
The track keeps its container fill; it is a control part, not a panel.
The elevated featured icon keeps its container wash, which reads in both themes and carries the icon's tone.
